page: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the ARM64 architecture using the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 model, operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, does not include local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier performance in single-core and multi-core processing, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2382.0 and a multi-core score of 25987.0. The architecture demonstrates high efficiency in text processing, software compilation with Clang, and data decompression, where bzip3 single-threaded decompression reached 17.26 GB/sec. Memory subsystem performance is strong for small-block cached read operations at 4319.78 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write operations fall into the average tier. Database operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the top tier, with static web serving reaching 92.57 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated physical cores and high-density ARMv9 architecture offer high compute throughput per resource unit, making it highly efficient for scale-out workloads. However, the lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, and the absence of AVX instruction sets may limit certain legacy x86 vector workloads. This instance is highly suited for software compilation, high-throughput web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded text processing tasks.
